texto: Aquella mañana, el Gnomo Bartolo llevó a Luna, Timo y Lin hasta la orilla del río brillante. Las tres tablas de roble que habían cortado el día anterior ya estaban listas, pero faltaba algo muy importante: las cuerdas de enredadera para sostener el puente. El agua corría rápido y hacía un ruido juguetón, como si quisiera probar su valentía.  —Hoy aprenderán a tensar sin romper —dijo Bartolo, acomodándose el sombrero—. Un buen puente no solo se ve fuerte, también sabe escuchar.  Luna abrió mucho los ojos. —¿Escuchar?  —Sí —respondió Timo, ajustándose las gafas—. Si una cuerda queda demasiado floja, el puente bosteza. Si queda demasiado apretada, se enoja.  Lin soltó tres burbujas azules, verdes y moradas que subieron despacito. Bartolo sonrió y les mostró cómo elegir enredaderas largas, suaves y resistentes. Primero las limpiaron de hojitas. Después las enrollaron. Luego las ataron a dos troncos gruesos, uno a cada lado del río. Pero cuando Luna quiso tensar la primera cuerda, ¡zas!, resbaló entre sus patas y cayó sentada sobre el musgo.  José Alejandro, seguro te habrías reído con ese plop tan gracioso. Luna también se rió, aunque después respiró hondo y volvió a intentarlo. Esta vez, Timo contó el ritmo: —Uno, dos, tira... uno, dos, tira...  Lin lanzó una burbuja grande que se posó justo en el centro de la cuerda. La burbuja no se movió ni a un lado ni al otro.  —¡Perfecta! —exclamó Bartolo—. Esa es la señal del equilibrio.  Trabajaron toda la tarde, cuerda por cuerda, hasta que el puente quedó sostenido y firme, aunque todavía sin barandas. Cuando el sol empezó a esconderse, Bartolo golpeó suavemente una cuerda y esta hizo un sonido dulce, como una nota de arpa.  —¿Lo oyen? —susurró—. El puente ya empezó a cantar.  Los tres amigos sonrieron orgullosos. Habían resuelto el trabajo del día. Mañana, con manos pacientes y ojos atentos, aprenderían a poner las barandas para que todos cruzaran seguros. Fin.
moraleja: La paciencia ayuda a encontrar el equilibrio.
pregunta: ¿Tú qué color de burbuja usarías para probar un puente, José Alejandro?

escenas.prompt: Gnome Bartolo with his pointed hat leading Luna the rabbit, Timo with glasses, and Lin the bubble-maker to the edge of a sparkling fast-flowing river, three oak planks lying ready on the mossy riverbank in morning light.
Bartolo the gnome demonstrating how to select and prepare long green vines while Luna, Timo and Lin watch carefully, cleaning leaves off the vines and rolling them up together near the river.

Luna the rabbit falling backwards onto soft moss as a vine slips from her paws, then trying again while Timo counts the rhythm and Lin releases a large shimmering bubble that floats perfectly balanced at the center of the stretched vine.

The completed rope bridge suspended over the sparkling river at sunset, Bartolo gently plucking one vine that glows and vibrates like a harp string, while Luna, Timo and Lin stand together proudly admiring their work in the golden light.

texto: In the green forest, Luna, Timo, and Lin met Eleanor again. It was map day. Eleanor had a small silver pencil. She smiled and said, "Today we draw a star map!"  Luna was happy. She loved to draw. Timo was calm and ready. Lin, the blue baby dragon, made pink bubbles. Pop, pop, pop.  Eleanor took them to a quiet hill. The sky was dark blue. One star was bright. Then two stars. Then many stars.  "Look up," said Eleanor. "Look slow. Count slow. Draw slow."  They sat on soft grass. Luna saw three bright stars. Timo saw a round moon. Lin saw one big star and laughed. "Big star! Big star!" he said.  Eleanor made a simple task. "Draw the moon. Draw the big star. Draw the tree near you. Then draw your path home."  Luna drew the moon first. Timo drew the tall tree. Lin could not draw well, but he helped. He made blue bubbles over the paper. The bubbles showed little shining circles. Eleanor said, "Good help, Lin!"  Then the wind came. The papers moved. Luna felt sad. "Oh no, my map!" she said.  Timo put a small stone on each paper. Lin made sticky gold bubbles. The papers stayed still. They worked again, slow and happy.  Soon, each friend had one little map. The maps were simple, but clear. Moon, star, tree, path. Moon, star, tree, path. José Alejandro, you can say the words too.  Eleanor looked at the three maps and smiled. "Today you made your first star map."  The work of the day was done. Tomorrow, they would use a map to find a hidden place. The end.
traduccion: Luna, Timo y Lin aprendieron a hacer un mapa sencillo mirando la luna, las estrellas y un árbol cercano. El viento casi arruina los dibujos, pero juntos encontraron una solución. Al final, terminaron su primer mapa de estrellas.
moraleja: Small steps make a clear path.
pregunta: José Alejandro, can you say: moon, star, tree?

escenas.prompt: In a green forest clearing, Eleanor the wise owl stands with Luna the rabbit, Timo the hedgehog, and Lin the small blue baby dragon who is making pink bubbles. Eleanor holds a small silver pencil and gestures welcomingly, surrounded by forest trees and soft morning light.

On a quiet hill under a dark blue night sky filled with bright stars and a round moon, Luna, Timo, and Lin sit on soft grass drawing on papers. A tall tree stands nearby. The three friends look up at the starry sky while Eleanor the owl watches them work, blue bubbles from Lin floating gently around them.

On the hill at night, Timo places small stones on the corners of papers while Lin creates sticky golden bubbles to keep the maps from blowing away in the wind. Luna looks relieved, and Eleanor smiles approvingly. The completed star maps showing moon, stars, tree and paths are visible on the papers.

texto: Nella piccola casa di Rosalinda c'era un buon profumo. Luna entrò piano. Timo guardò i barattoli. Lin, il drago blu bebé, fece bolle gialle e rosa. Rosalinda sorrise.  —Oggi facciamo biscotti magici —disse piano—. Sono biscotti della risata.  Luna batté le mani. —Che bello!  Rosalinda mise gli ingredienti sul tavolo. C'erano farina, miele, latte, e una polvere d'arancia molto fine. C'era anche una ciotola blu.  —Prima, mescoliamo bene —disse Rosalinda.  Luna mescolò la farina e il latte. Timo aggiunse il miele. Lin guardò la pasta con occhi grandi. Poi fece una bolla azzurra. La bolla scese piano nella ciotola.  —Perfetto —disse Rosalinda—. La bolla porta allegria.  Poi fecero dieci biscotti piccoli. Uno, due, tre... fino a dieci. José Alejandro, anche tu potevi contare con loro. I biscotti erano tondi e morbidi.  Ma c'era un problema. Il forno magico era freddo. Nessuna luce, nessun calore. Luna era triste. —Oh no, niente biscotti.  Timo pensò un momento. —Forse il forno ha sonno.  Rosalinda rise piano. —Forse sì. Serve una canzone dolce.  Allora Luna cantò una nota chiara. Timo cantò una nota bassa. Lin fece tre bolle brillanti. Pop, pop, pop. Il forno si svegliò. Fece una luce arancione calda.  I biscotti entrarono nel forno. Dopo poco, uscì un profumo dolce. Rosalinda diede un biscotto a ciascuno. Luna lo mangiò e rise. Timo rise. Anche Lin rise, e fece bolle che ballavano.  Il lavoro del giorno era finito. I biscotti della risata erano pronti. Domani, forse, cucineranno qualcosa che canta. Fine.
traduccion: Luna, Timo y Lin prepararon galletas mágicas de la risa con Rosalinda. El horno no quería encenderse, pero lo despertaron con una canción y burbujas brillantes. Al final, las galletas salieron perfectas y todos rieron felices.
moraleja: Con alegría, anche i problemi si sciolgono.
pregunta: José Alejandro, tu preferisci biscotti al miele o al latte?

escenas.prompt: Inside Rosalinda's cozy cottage kitchen, Rosalinda the kind witch smiling at Luna the little rabbit, Timo the gray mouse looking at glass jars on shelves, and Lin the baby blue dragon blowing yellow and pink bubbles, warm lighting and magical atmosphere

Luna the rabbit mixing flour and milk in a blue bowl on wooden table, Timo the mouse pouring honey, Lin the baby blue dragon adding a glowing blue bubble into the mixture, ingredients scattered around including orange powder, Rosalinda watching happily

Luna, Timo and Lin laughing joyfully while eating round cookies, the magical oven glowing warm orange in the background, Lin blowing dancing sparkling bubbles that float around, cheerful and celebratory atmosphere in the cottage

texto: A la mañana siguiente, Luna, Timo y Lin llegaron muy temprano al taller del Gnomo Bartolo. El viejo gnomo los esperaba con una carretilla de madera.  —Buenos días, aprendices —dijo con una sonrisa—. Hoy buscaremos la madera perfecta para el puente. ¿Saben cuál es?  Luna movió sus orejas pensando. Timo ajustó sus gafitas. Y Lin, el dragoncito azul bebé, soltó una burbuja enorme que flotó hasta el cielo.  —¿Madera fuerte? —preguntó Luna.  —¡Exacto! —respondió Bartolo—. Necesitamos roble del Bosque Viejo. Es pesado, pero dura muchos, muchos años.  Caminaron juntos por senderos angostos hasta llegar al Bosque Viejo. Allí los árboles eran enormes, con troncos gruesos como casas. Bartolo golpeó un tronco caído con su martillo.  —Escuchen —dijo.  El sonido fue profundo, como un tambor. Bartolo sonrió.  —Este roble es perfecto. ¿Me ayudan a marcarlo?  Luna sostuvo la cuerda. Timo midió con una vara larga. Y Lin, ¿sabes qué hizo, José Alejandro? ¡Escupió burbujas de colores para que Bartolo supiera dónde cortar!  Entre todos cortaron tres tablas largas. Eran muy pesadas, pero trabajando juntos lograron llevarlas de vuelta al taller.  —Mañana aprenderemos a hacer las cuerdas —dijo Bartolo mientras el sol se ponía—. Hoy hicieron un gran trabajo.  Luna, Timo y Lin se fueron a casa cansados, pero felices. Habían encontrado la madera perfecta para su puente. Fin.
moraleja: El trabajo en equipo hace que las tareas difíciles se vuelvan posibles.
pregunta: José Alejandro, ¿qué árbol crees que es más fuerte: el roble o el pino?

escenas.prompt: Luna the little rabbit, Timo the small mouse with glasses, and Lin the baby blue dragon arrive at Gnome Bartolo's wooden workshop in early morning. The old gnome with a white beard welcomes them beside a wooden wheelbarrow filled with lumber, sunlight streaming through the windows.

The group walks through a narrow forest path into the Ancient Forest where enormous oak trees tower overhead with trunks as thick as houses. Gnome Bartolo kneels beside a fallen oak trunk, tapping it with his hammer while Luna, Timo, and Lin watch curiously.

Luna holds a rope, Timo measures with a long stick, and Lin the baby blue dragon spits colorful bubbles to mark where to cut on the fallen oak trunk. Gnome Bartolo works with his tools as the three friends help him prepare three long wooden planks in the forest.

Luna, Timo, Lin, and Gnome Bartolo carry three heavy oak planks back to the workshop at sunset, working together with tired but happy expressions. The warm orange sky glows behind them as they approach the cozy wooden workshop.

texto: The next morning, Luna, Timo and Lin went to see Eleanor. She was waiting near the big oak tree.  —Good morning, little friends! —said Eleanor—. Today we count steps. Do you know why?  Luna shook her head. Timo looked curious. Lin, the little blue dragon baby, blew happy bubbles.  —To make a good map, we need to know how far we walk —Eleanor said.  She gave Luna a small red flag.  —Put this flag here. Now, walk to that tree and count every step.  Luna walked slowly. One, two, three… she counted to twenty steps. She put the flag near the tree.  —Very good! —said Eleanor—. Now, Timo, you count steps to the river.  Timo walked and counted. One, two, three… fifteen steps. José Alejandro, Timo counted fifteen steps to the river!  Lin wanted to help too. He walked and blew bubbles. One bubble for every step! The bubbles floated in a line.  —Perfect! —said Eleanor—. Tomorrow we draw our first map. You are learning very fast.  Luna, Timo and Lin smiled. Counting steps was fun! They went home happy, counting every step back home. The end.
traduccion: Eleanor enseña a Luna, Timo y Lin a contar pasos para hacer mapas. Luna cuenta 20 pasos hasta un árbol, Timo cuenta 15 hasta el río, y Lin hace burbujas mientras camina. Mañana dibujarán su primer mapa.
moraleja: Small steps help us measure big places.
pregunta: José Alejandro, how many steps from your bed to the kitchen?

escenas.prompt: Eleanor the wise owl standing near a big oak tree, explaining to Luna the rabbit, Timo the fox cub, and Lin the tiny blue dragon baby, morning forest setting with sunlight filtering through leaves and a small red flag in Eleanor's wing.

Luna the rabbit walking carefully with a small red flag counting steps toward a distant tree, while Timo the fox cub walks counting steps toward a sparkling river, forest meadow with flowers and grass.

Lin the baby blue dragon blowing cheerful colorful bubbles that float in a line marking his counted steps, Luna the rabbit and Timo the fox cub watching happily, Eleanor the owl smiling proudly, warm afternoon forest atmosphere.

texto: La mattina dopo, Luna, Timo e Lin tornarono alla casetta di Rosalinda. La strega buona preparava una pentola grande.  —Buongiorno, piccoli cuochi! —disse Rosalinda—. Oggi facciamo la zuppa dei sogni. Volete aiutarmi?  —Sì! —dissero tutti insieme.  Rosalinda mostrò tre ingredienti: foglie di menta, carote dolci e petali di rosa.  —Mettete le carote nella pentola —disse.  Luna mise le carote. Timo aggiunse le foglie di menta. E Lin, il piccolo drago azzurro, soffiò bolle colorate nella pentola!  —Perfetto! —rise Rosalinda—. Le bolle di Lin fanno la magia!  Mescolarono tutti insieme. La zuppa diventò color rosa brillante. José Alejandro, era bellissima!  —Questa zuppa è speciale —spiegò Rosalinda—. Chi la mangia fa sogni belli tutta la notte.  Luna assaggiò un cucchiaio. Era dolce e calda.  —Buonissima! —disse Luna.  Rosalinda diede a ognuno un vasetto di zuppa.  —Portatela a casa. Domani cuciniamo biscotti che fanno ridere.  Luna, Timo e Lin tornarono a casa felici con i loro vasetti magici. Quella notte fecero sogni bellissimi. Fine.
traduccion: Rosalinda enseña a Luna, Timo y Lin a hacer la sopa de los sueños con hojas de menta, zanahorias y pétalos de rosa. Las burbujas de Lin hacen la magia. Quien la come tiene sueños hermosos toda la noche.
moraleja: La cucina fatta con amore porta felicità.
pregunta: José Alejandro, che sogno bello vorresti fare stanotte?

escenas.prompt: Inside Rosalinda the kind witch's cozy cottage, a large pot sits on the stove. Luna the rabbit, Timo the squirrel, and Lin the small blue dragon watch as Rosalinda shows them three magical ingredients: mint leaves, sweet carrots, and rose petals on a wooden table.

Luna drops carrots into the steaming pot while Timo adds mint leaves. Lin the blue dragon blows colorful magical bubbles into the pot, making the soup turn bright pink. Rosalinda stirs the magical dream soup with a wooden spoon, everyone smiling together in the warm kitchen.

Luna the rabbit, Timo the squirrel, and Lin the blue dragon sleep peacefully in their beds at night, each holding a small jar of pink dream soup. Soft dreamy clouds with stars and magical sparkles float above them, showing their beautiful dreams coming true.

titulo: Capítulo 1 · El Puente Roto y el Gnomo Bartolo
texto: Una mañana soleada, Luna la conejita, Timo el búho con gafitas y Lin, el pequeño dragón azul que escupía burbujas de colores, corrían felices hacia el río. Querían cruzar al Prado de las Flores, pero cuando llegaron... ¡oh no! El puente de madera estaba roto en el medio.  —¿Y ahora cómo cruzaremos? —preguntó Luna, triste.  Lin soltó una burbuja dorada que flotó hasta el otro lado, pero eso no les servía para pasar.  De pronto, escucharon una voz ronca:  —¡Vaya, vaya! ¿Necesitan un puente nuevo, pequeños?  Era Bartolo, un gnomo anciano con barba blanca, sombrero puntiagudo verde y un cinturón lleno de herramientas.  —Soy constructor de puentes desde hace cien años —dijo con orgullo—. Si me ayudan esta semana, les enseñaré mi oficio.  —¡Sí! —gritaron los tres.  Bartolo sacó un rollo de papel y un lápiz.  —Primero, hay que medir. Un puente debe ser fuerte y equilibrado. Timo, ¿ves esa roca? Cuenta cuántos pasos hay desde aquí hasta allá.  Timo voló contando: ¡uno, dos, tres... quince pasos!  —Perfecto. Mañana cortaremos la madera. Hoy solo observaremos el río: su ancho, su corriente, sus secretos.  Luna, Timo y Lin miraron el agua con atención. ¿Sabes qué vieron, José Alejandro? Pequeños peces plateados, piedras redondas y ramas que bailaban con la corriente.  —Un buen constructor —dijo Bartolo— primero observa, luego piensa, después construye.  Así terminó el primer día. Los tres amigos se fueron a casa soñando con el puente que pronto nacería bajo sus manos. Fin.
moraleja: Antes de construir algo grande, primero hay que observar con paciencia.
pregunta: ¿Tú has visto algún puente cerca de tu casa, José Alejandro? ¿De qué crees que está hecho?

escenas.prompt: Luna the little rabbit, Timo the owl with glasses, and Lin the small blue dragon running happily toward a river on a sunny morning, discovering a broken wooden bridge in the middle, with Lin blowing a golden bubble that floats across the water

Bartolo the elderly gnome with white beard, green pointy hat and tool belt full of construction tools, appearing before the three friends and unrolling a paper blueprint while explaining his craft as a bridge builder
Timo the owl flying and counting steps from one side to the other (fifteen steps), while Bartolo the gnome points and measures, and Luna and Lin watch attentively from the riverbank

Luna, Timo and Lin observing the river carefully, seeing small silver fish, round stones and branches dancing in the current, while Bartolo the gnome teaches them to observe first, then think, then build, as the sun sets and the three friends walk home dreaming of their future bridge

titulo: Chapter 1 · Eleanor and the First Lesson of Looking
texto: One bright afternoon, Luna the bunny, Timo the owl with little glasses, and Lin, the baby blue dragon who blew colorful bubbles, were playing hide-and-seek near the Great Oak Tree. Suddenly, they heard soft singing above them.  Looking up, they saw a fairy with silver wings and a backpack full of rolled papers.  "Hello, little ones! I'm Eleanor, the Wandering Fairy. I travel the forest drawing maps of every path, stream, and secret place."  "Maps? What are those?" asked Luna, curious.  Eleanor smiled and unrolled a beautiful paper covered in drawings: trees, rivers, mountains, and tiny stars.  "A map shows where things are. It helps travelers find their way home, discover treasures, or remember special places."  Lin blew a purple bubble of excitement.  "This week, I'll teach you to make your own map of the forest," Eleanor said. "But first, you must learn the most important skill: looking."  "Looking?" Timo adjusted his glasses. "We already know how to look!"  "Ah, but do you really see?" Eleanor winked. "Close your eyes, then open them and tell me five things around us."  They tried. Luna noticed mushrooms shaped like umbrellas. Timo saw a spider's web sparkling with dew. Lin spotted three different types of flowers.  "Excellent! You know, José Alejandro, just like you when you explore your neighborhood, these three friends are learning to notice the magical details hidden everywhere."  Eleanor gave each of them a blank paper and a charcoal pencil.  "Tomorrow, we'll start drawing. Today, just observe. Count the trees between here and the stream. Notice their shapes. A map-maker sees the world with curious eyes."  The three friends walked home slowly, looking at everything as if for the first time. The end.
traduccion: Una tarde brillante, Luna, Timo y Lin conocieron a Eleanor, un hada viajera que dibuja mapas mágicos. Ella les enseñó la primera lección: observar de verdad. Cerraron los ojos y luego buscaron cinco detalles a su alrededor. Eleanor les dio papel y lápiz, y les pidió que mañana empezarían a dibujar, pero hoy solo debían mirar con ojos curiosos.
moraleja: To make a map of the world, first learn to truly see it.
pregunta: José Alejandro, if you were to draw a map of your room, what five special things would you include?

escenas.prompt: Luna the bunny, Timo the owl with little glasses, and Lin the baby blue dragon playing hide-and-seek near a giant oak tree, looking up in wonder at Eleanor the fairy with silver wings and a backpack full of papers hovering above them in the sunlight

Eleanor the fairy unrolling a beautiful hand-drawn map covered in trees, rivers, and mountains while Luna, Timo, and Lin gather around excitedly discovering magical forest details: umbrella-shaped mushrooms, a dewdrop-covered spider web, and colorful wildflowers

Luna, Timo, and Lin walking slowly through the forest path toward a sparkling stream, each holding blank paper and charcoal pencils, looking carefully at trees and nature around them with newfound curious eyes as the afternoon sun filters through the leaves

titulo: Capitolo 1 · La Casetta Profumata di Rosalinda
texto: Un pomeriggio di primavera, Luna la coniglietta, Timo il gufetto con gli occhialini e Lin, il draghetto blu bebè che sputava bolle colorate, passeggiavano nel bosco quando sentirono un profumo dolcissimo.  «Che buon odore!» disse Luna, muovendo il nasino.  Seguirono il profumo fino a una casetta rotonda coperta di fiori viola e gialli. Dalla finestra usciva un fumo argentato.  Bussarono: TOC TOC TOC.  La porta si aprì e apparve una strega con cappello a punta azzurro, grembiule pieno di stelle e un sorriso gentile.  «Benvenuti, piccoli! Sono Rosalinda, la strega buona. Sto preparando il tè di camomilla brillante. Volete imparare?»  «Una strega buona?» chiese Timo, curioso.  «Certo! Io cucino piatti magici con fiori, miele, foglie aromatiche e luce di luna. Ogni ricetta ha un piccolo incantesimo di gioia.»  Lin soffiò una bolla verde di entusiasmo.  Rosalinda li fece entrare. La cucina era piena di vasetti colorati, cucchiai di legno e pentole che cantavano.  «Oggi prepariamo il tè più semplice: camomilla brillante. Serve per dormire bene e fare sogni felici.»  Prese tre fiori di camomilla, li mise in una teiera di cristallo e aggiunse acqua calda.  «Ora, il tocco magico: bisogna sussurrare un desiderio gentile alla teiera.»  Luna sussurrò: «Che tutti dormano bene stanotte.»  Il tè cominciò a brillare come stelline dorate!  «Perfetto!» disse Rosalinda. «Sai, José Alejandro, cucinare con amore è la vera magia. Domani impareremo una ricetta più difficile: i biscotti al miele di stelle.»  I tre amici tornarono a casa con una tazza di tè brillante ciascuno, pronti per sogni meravigliosi. Fine.
traduccion: Una tarde de primavera, Luna, Timo y Lin siguieron un aroma dulce hasta la casita de Rosalinda, una bruja buena que cocina platos mágicos. Ella les enseñó a preparar té de manzanilla brillante: flores, agua caliente y un deseo gentil susurrado. El té comenzó a brillar como estrellitas doradas. Rosalinda les dijo que cocinar con amor es la verdadera magia.
moraleja: Cucinare con amore è la magia più dolce di tutte.
pregunta: José Alejandro, se tu potessi preparare un tè magico, che desiderio gentile sussurreresti?

escenas.prompt: Luna the little rabbit, Timo the owlet with tiny glasses, and Lin the baby blue dragon walking through a spring forest, discovering a round cottage covered in purple and yellow flowers with silver smoke coming from the window.

Inside the magical kitchen, Rosalinda the kind witch with blue pointed hat and star-patterned apron shows Luna, Timo and Lin her colorful jars, wooden spoons and singing pots, while holding chamomile flowers and a crystal teapot.

Luna the rabbit whispers to the crystal teapot while Timo and Lin watch amazed as the chamomile tea begins to glow with golden sparkles like little stars, Rosalinda smiling warmly beside them in her cozy magical kitchen.
